title: Chocolate Fudge Cake
subtitle: a deeply chocolatey layer cake with glossy ganache
excerpt: A rich, damp chocolate cake sandwiched and coated with dark chocolate ganache. Oil keeps the crumb moist for days. The ganache is just chocolate and cream -- simple and very good.
sourceNotes: Chocolate fudge cake is a standard of British cafe and home baking. The method draws on American devil's food cake techniques.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the plain cake layers without ganache. Assemble from frozen, ganache on, then defrost.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake layers a day ahead. Make ganache on the day and assemble.

content.text: The batter for this cake is very liquid -- more liquid than most cake batters. This is correct. The hot water (or coffee) in the batter blooms the cocoa and makes the chocolate flavour deeper. Do not worry about the consistency when it goes in the tin.

items.prepNote: use 200g dark chocolate (70%) for the ganache -- broken into pieces
for ganache -- heat and pour over the chocolate, stir until smooth

content.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Grease and line two 20cm round tins.
Sift together the flour, cocoa, baking powder, bicarb, sugar, and a pinch of salt. In a jug, whisk together the eggs, oil, milk, and vanilla. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and mix until smooth.
Pour in 150ml of just-boiled water or hot coffee and stir to combine. The batter will be very thin. Divide evenly between the tins.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes before turning out. Leave to cool fully.

Make the ganache: heat the cream until just below boiling. Pour over the broken chocolate. Leave for 2 minutes, then stir until smooth. Cool until spreadable (about 30 minutes). Sandwich and coat the cake.

items.symptom: Ganache is too runny to spread
items.fix: Leave at room temperature until it holds a ribbon when stirred -- about 30 to 45 minutes. Speed it up by placing in the fridge for 10 minutes.

items.symptom: Cake layers are very domed and difficult to sandwich
items.cause: Common with very liquid batters. The dome can be levelled.
items.fix: Use a serrated knife to trim the dome flat before sandwiching. Keep the trimmings for a cook's treat.

content.text: Chocolate fudge cake is the chocolate cake of British cafes, birthdays, and bake sales. It is richer and more intensely flavoured than a chocolate sponge. The ganache finish is borrowed from French patisserie but has been fully absorbed into British baking culture. It is the kind of cake people request for their birthday.
